answer: In an agent marketplace selling tundra surveys, each seller identity must lock $100 for 30 days before bidding, and each identity can hold only one active job. An agent hired to map a knoll at dawn faces the same rule as every other seller. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore requires locking $100,000, not merely generating keys. The defense does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying bidding capacity consume real capital.
